Figure 5B shows that the proliferative zone indicated by Ki67 expression expands towards the top of the glands, while the bases remain largely non-proliferative. in_text_mentions: Significant tumor heterogeneity was observed in 6 cases. In 2 cases, tumor heterogeneity was observed in both IHC and DISH (cases 1 and 6) (Fig. 3). In 4 cases, tumor heterogeneity was observed only in IHC (cases 3, 4, 5, 9). In 2 cases, discrepant results between TMA and whole-tissue analysis were seen (cases 1 and 4). Both cases demonstrated tumor heterogeneity by IHC, DISH, or both. Results are shown in Table 3.

panels.rationale: Single upper-endoscopy image from a human patient annotating the endoscopic landmarks (Z line, endoscopic GEJ, and endoscopic CLE). The visible columnar-lined esophageal segment between the squamocolumnar junction and GEJ corresponds to the salmon-pink columnar mucosa finding associated with Barrett esophagus; it is a real patient endoscopic image with direct caption support.
panels.attribution_text: Baruah et al. Understanding the Columnar Lined Esophagus and Its Variations in Length With Age: A Cadaveric Study.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.46095. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Endoscopic landmarks for determining the CLE. Endoscopic picture provided by Dr. PKD Phukan, General Surgeon. CLE: columnar lined epithelium.
in_text_mentions: unction between the pale pearly colored squamous epithelium and the salmon-colored columnar epithelium. The GEJ is usually identified as a pinch at the distal end of the esophagus, coinciding with the most proximal appearance of the gastric rugal folds. This point marks the beginning of the stomach and its distance from the Z line conventionally corresponds to the CLE [4,11]. Endoscopically the AZ distance/length of CLE can be measured by subtracting the distance of the incisor to the squamocolumnar junction (Z line) from the distance of the incisor to the gastroesophageal junction (Figure 3).

plate_findings.evidence: MUC2 immunostaining shows intestinal predominant mucin phenotype in Barrett esophagus

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: IHC image demonstrating MUC2 expression indicating intestinal metaplasia in Barrett esophagus tissue. B: IHC image demonstrating CDX2 expression, a marker of intestinal metaplasia in Barrett esophagus. C: IHC image showing COX-2 positive expression related to carcinogenesis in Barrett esophagus tissue. D: IHC image showing CD34 staining of microvessels indicating angiogenesis grade in Barrett mucosa. E: IHC image showing PCNA positive staining indicating cellular proliferation in Barrett esophagus tissue.

in_text_mentions: c mucin (45MI, 1:100, Novocastra, Newcastle, UK) and MUC2 (Ccp58, 1:100, Novocastra) were used for phenotyping, as previously described.28–30 When Barrett epithelial cells were more dominantly stained by the anti-MUC2 antibody than the antihuman gastric mucin antibody, the case was diagnosed as BE with the intestinal predominant mucin phenotype (Figure 3A). Caudal-type homeobox transcription factor 2 (CDX2) (CDX2-88, 1:100, BioGenex, San Ramon, CA) was used as immunostaining markers of intestinal metaplasia, and judged to be positive when the stained area was greater than 50% (Figure 3B).28,29
